You have never heard of this show. You just watched this whole clip (descriptions in brackets are what is on screen; speakers are described by how they look):

a figure in period dress: "Every wedding needs a widow. Why not two?"
[Hard cut]
[On screen: Close-up on the widow's jaw tightening.]
a figure in period dress: "Why does the sea give back only what it wants?"

a man in period dress: "Your father paid me to watch over you."
[Sound: The crowd gasps.]
[On screen: Slow push-in on the figure in period dress as the lamp flickers behind them.]

a figure in period dress: "Expose me and her father hangs beside me."
[On screen: Wide shot of the storm-lashed harbour, lanterns swinging on the quay.]
[Action: the figure in period dress kneels on the slick quay boards.]
[On screen: Close-up on the widow's hands gripping the rail.]
a figure in period dress: "Smile, sister. It is your last night of freedom."
[On screen: Extreme close-up on the figure in period dress's eyes, wet with sea spray.]
a man in period dress: "I saw who slipped the ring into your shawl."
[On screen: Wide shot of the storm-lashed harbour, lanterns swinging on the quay.]
a man in period dress: "Your father paid me to watch over you."
[On screen: Close-up on the figure in period dress's jaw tightening.]
[On screen: Over-the-shoulder shot from the man in period dress toward the figure in period dress.]
a figure in period dress: "The council has already decided her fate."
[On screen: Wide shot of the storm-lashed harbour, lanterns swinging on the quay.]
[Action: the the figure in period dress tears the lace veil and lets it fall.]
a figure in period dress: "Every wedding needs a widow. Why not two?"
